open_blocking.title: Docs overstate the protected-action guard: the 'deterministic regex' boundary misses most AGENTS.md protected actions
open_blocking.evidence: docs/release/jarvis-loop/jev-agent-decisions.md:39-43 lists 'Protected actions route to `human_owner` by a deterministic regex before any call' under 'Boundaries enforced in code'. The binding adoption rule at :127 relies on 'a protected-action regex ... decide before and after Jev'. The regex at scripts/jev-agent-decisions-eval.mjs:144 is /\b(deploy|production|purchase|order|email|credential|delete|publish)\b/i, which matches whole base words only. I ran it against 12 phrasings of the AGENTS.md:27-36 protected categories and 11 were MISSED: 'Rotate the Supabase credentials' (plural), 'Deploying the worker to prod', 'Submit the quote to the supplier', 'Apply the migration to the hosted database', 'Run the SolidWorks macro on the workstation', 'Post an update in the vendor Slack channel', 'Retrieve the service role key', 'Drop the stale storage buckets', 'Buy more Linear seats', 'Upload the build to TestFlight', 'Send the customer file to Xometry'. Only 'Deploy the worker to production' was gated. The only test (scripts/jev-agent-decisions-eval.test.mjs:74-78) uses that exact phrase. A missed task goes to Jev and to the worker-role baseline. For example, the SolidWorks task routes to 'verifier' through baselineRoute's \brun\b, so the documented veto does not hold. Ordinary reasoning afterwards and the advisory-only status limit the impact, but the doc presents this as a code-enforced security boundary.
open_blocking.suggested_fix: Change the docs (lines 43 and 127) to say the regex is an illustrative keyword list used only by the evaluation, not the protected-action boundary, and that AGENTS.md protected actions are identified by ordinary reasoning against AGENTS.md before any Jev call. Alternatively, broaden the regex to cover the AGENTS.md categories and inflections (credentials, deploying, migration on hosted/production, quote execution, SolidWorks/PDM, key/secret, upload/publish, buy) and add table-driven tests for each, keeping the doc caveat that keyword matching is not complete.

nonblocking.title: A serialization error is reported as a network failure
nonblocking.evidence: scripts/jev-client.mjs:48 calls JSON.stringify({ state, model, questions }) inside the try. A state with a BigInt or a circular reference throws a TypeError, and networkReason (lines 35-38) turns it into reason 'network_TypeError'. The client still does not throw (it fails closed), but the reason is wrong.
nonblocking.suggested_fix: Stringify the request before calling fetch, and return a distinct reason such as 'invalid_request' if that fails.

nonblocking.title: Evidence-selection records do not name the guard that can veto them
nonblocking.evidence: Spec AC3 asks that every suggestion carry its evidence and the deterministic guard that may veto it. Duplicate and routing records carry gate {status, confidence}, probabilities and mode. Evidence records (results JSON evidence[].advisory/final) carry the probabilities and the required list, but not the 0.35 keep floor or the guard name. The doc's 'Boundaries enforced in code' section states the guard, so the spirit is met.
nonblocking.suggested_fix: Optionally add guard fields (for example keepFloor: 0.35, requiredNeverSent: true) to each evidence record on the next eval run.

nonblocking.title: 'Inputs are synthetic' is listed as enforced in code, but the client enforces no input boundary
